core_obligations: Separatedness (proof lines 2213-2227): given two elements of the plus construction which agree after restriction along a covering, the author chooses coverings presenting both and a common refinement, finds representatives of both elements on the members of the refinement, and uses the separatedness of the given presheaf on the further common refinement to conclude that the two elements coincide.

Sheaf and injectivity (proof lines 2230-2249): the canonical map is injective and refinements give injective maps on compatible families; for a compatible family in the plus construction the author chooses local representatives, checks they agree on the pairwise products by the sheaf condition, amalgamates them in the plus construction and leaves to the reader the check that the amalgamation restricts to the given family.
Isomorphism and iteration (proof lines 2252-2258): for a sheaf the canonical map is an isomorphism directly from the definitions, and the last statement then follows.
proof_roadmap: Prove separatedness by reducing to a common refinement and using separatedness of the presheaf.
Prove the sheaf property and injectivity of the canonical map using local presentations.
Read off the remaining two statements from the definitions.
difficulty_reason: The theorem collects the fundamental properties of the plus construction: it is separated, it is a sheaf with injective canonical map when the presheaf is separated, the canonical map is an isomorphism for sheaves, and iterating it once more always gives a sheaf (statement lines 2191-2210). The proof is a complete argument: separatedness is obtained by choosing presentations of the two elements and a common refinement and using the separatedness of the presheaf (proof lines 2213-2227); the sheaf property and injectivity are proved by choosing local representatives of a compatible family, checking compatibility on the pairwise products and amalgamating in the plus construction, with the author leaving to the reader only the final restriction check (proof lines 2230-2249); and the last two statements follow directly from the definitions (proof lines 2252-2258). The non-formal content is the two constructions and the amalgamation. The claim is H2: the parts are written out with each input named.
